title: Stash tabs you can customise
notes: The stash tabs are yours to arrange. The ✎ button at the end of the tab row lets you add tabs (up to ten), rename them, move them up and down, change what each one is, and delete them (the gear in a deleted tab goes to your other tabs).

Tab types: Items (any gear, a full grid like the main stash), Uniques (Legendary and Set gear only), Currency, Gems and Runes. There is one Currency, one Gems and one Runes tab at most. The main stash always stays the first Items tab.

Gear you put away goes to a Uniques tab first if it is Legendary or Set, otherwise to the first Items tab with room. Your tabs are shared by every character, like the rest of the stash, and traded items are cleared out of every tab.

title: Meta supports: cast on crit, cast when damaged
notes: Two new support gems, found like the others: Cast on Critical Strike and Cast when Damage Taken. Link one in a skill slot and a new cell appears after the links: tap it at the stash or Jeweler to choose which of your skills it casts.

That skill is cast for free, without its cooldown or cost, whenever you land a critical strike (at most every 0.4 seconds) or take damage (at most every second). It never triggers another triggered skill, and a skill that moves you (a leap or a dash) cannot be chosen.
A skill can carry one meta support, and hirelings cannot use them.

title: Skill Gems and gem cutting
notes: Skill gems no longer drop one per skill, and the Merchant no longer sells them. A plain Skill Gem drops from elites (and, rarely, normal monsters), and from every boss.

Open the Skills window (the 💠 button) and switch to Gem Cutting: every skill is listed under Bow, Melee, Spell, Throwing or Shouts & Buffs with what it needs. Cut a Skill Gem into the skill you want to unlock it for that character for good.
A skill you have unlocked can be put in any skill slot and taken out again; it is not used up. Characters you already had keep every skill they had.
Skill Gems are shared by your whole account, but each character unlocks its own skills.

title: Passive tree: choose your attributes
notes: The small Strength, Dexterity, Vitality and Energy nodes of the passive tree are now Attribute nodes: tap one and pick which attribute it gives. They show four coloured quarters until you take them.
A node you had already taken keeps the attribute it gave before. Refunding a node, or a respec, forgets its choice.

title: Currency drops one by one
notes: Currency no longer piles up under one "Currency (N)" label. Every orb, shard, scroll, gem and rune drops as its own item on the ground.
Tap any currency and you pick it up together with all the currency lying near it. One message tells you what you got.

title: Skills button and skill hotkeys in town
notes: A new Skills button sits beside the passive tree button, top right. It opens your skills window.

In town, tap one of your skill buttons and a list of the skills you can put there drops down. Tap a skill to equip it. A skill that is already on another button moves: it comes off the old button and goes on the new one, and what was on the new button goes back to your pouch. Skills you can't use yet are greyed out with what they need.
Support gems are still linked at the Jeweler.

title: Act I balance: levels and bosses
notes: Act I now takes a new character to about level 12 to 17. Monsters in its zones give far less experience than they did, and its quests and bosses give a fixed amount, so the pace no longer runs away in the later zones.

The bosses of Act I are much tougher: they have many times the life, so a fight lasts from about half a minute to a couple of minutes (Lord Malaphax the longest), and they hit harder, so standing still will not win it. Their rewards are unchanged.
Fixed: in the Ashen Verge the boss health bar did not move to the Rift Golem once the Grave Warden had been slain and had faded away.

title: Act I phase 6: world events and mini-dungeons
notes: Four new events in the open zones: a Cursed Shrine (cleanse it against three waves of fiends for loot and a two-minute blessing), Tears in Reality (a rift that pulls you in and spews elites: destroy its three spires before it bursts), The Dying Pilgrim (keep the paladin above half his life against waves of rot fiends and a hidden reliquary opens) and the Pyre of the Dead (burn the corpses before they rise, and survive the horde that the fire enrages).

Mini-dungeons: now and then a trapdoor, cave mouth or stone grate appears in the Wilds, the Hollow, the Fen or the Verge. The Rot-Damp Cellar (maggots, and a mimic on a hoard), the Forgotten Bone Pit (step into the middle and the portcullises fall, and a skeleton champion comes for you), the Hermit's Sanctum (a quiet cave and a bench that gives one free reroll of an item's modifiers or sockets) and the Weeping Fissure (pitch dark, crowded, and a Tainted Chest tethered to three elite guardians).
This completes the Act I story and its side content.

title: Act I phase 5: the Sepulcher of Mourning and Lord Malaphax
notes: The great door at the end of the Lower Ossuary opens, once you have broken the third Veil Anchor, onto the Sepulcher of Mourning: a sunken cathedral with broken stained glass, a floor flooded under coagulated blood that slows you, and a massive torn rift in the altar wall.

New main quest, The Flesh-Torn: Lord Malaphax, once Duke Edward of Oakhaven, waits before the rift. His first face is iron: great cleaves, a crushing blow and ground-tears of boiled blood. At half his life he tears the armour off and fights with scythes, dashes and falling ceiling. Then the Veil Realm: the screen goes dark, shadows tear at you, and you must find and destroy the Rift Soul to end it. At a fifth of his life there are two souls at once.
Finishing the quest completes Act I. Lord Malaphax can be fought again afterwards for his drops.

title: Act I phase 4: the Grand Ossuary
notes: The Ossuary's gates in the Ashen Verge now lead down into the Grand Ossuary, two levels of narrow stone halls, sarcophagi, torches and soul lanterns. Beware the spike traps in the hallways: watch the stone shiver, then go.

New main quest, Descent into Madness: High Priestess Althea sends you down to shatter three Veil Anchors, each channelled by a cultist herald. Every anchor you break shakes the floor and brings an elite ambush out of the dark. The heralds are boss fights you can repeat once the quest is done.
New side quest, Restless Ancestors: a weeping spirit on the first level wants her four stolen urns back from the open sarcophagi. Her reward is a lasting +5% to all resistances.
The key from The Last Watch now opens the armory vault behind a cracked wall in the first level's guardroom, once, for three rare items.
New monsters: Skeleton Vanguards and Veil Cultists. The Lower Ossuary ends at a great barred door. What lies behind it comes in the next update.

title: Act I phase 3: the Ashen Verge
notes: A new zone: the Ashen Verge, the autumn woods burnt out to ash, with graveyards, outer ruins, Bleed Rifts that spill armoured fiends, and a mausoleum on raised ground. The gate at the far end of the Weeping Hollow now opens onto it, and so does the road east out of the Sunken Fen.

New main quest, Breaking the Seal: High Priestess Althea needs the two halves of the Warded Keystone. One is held by the Maddened Grave Warden, who raises the dead; the other by the Rift Golem, which tears the rift open to bring fiends through. Join them at the sealed mausoleum. Both are boss fights you can repeat once the quest is done.

New side quest, The Last Watch: Scout Captain Dennis lost three scouts in the Verge. Put down the two the Taint twisted and find the one who is still alive in the watchtower. The reward includes a key to a vault, kept for later.
The Ossuary's gates open at the end of Breaking the Seal, onto a stair into the dark. What lies below comes in the next update.

title: Act I phase 2: the Weeping Hollow and the Sunken Fen
notes: Two new zones off the Blackroot Wilds: the Weeping Hollow, caves under the Wilds (a cave mouth east of the ruined manor), with a tainted river you cross by bridges, and the Sunken Fen, drowned woodland to the south, where patches of mire slow you and the monsters alike.

New main quest, Poisoning the Well: once the first chapter is done, High Priestess Althea sends you into the Hollow to find the Brood Cyst, slay its guardian Skittering Matron Vhol and plant the Alchemical Purge Ward. She is a real boss fight: she charges, lashes, spits and calls her brood.
New side quest, A Taste for Rot: Apothecary Voss hides in the Fen and wants the glands of three Fen Crawlers. He pays in a choice: his draught (+4 attribute points) or a rune.
The vine-choked gate at the far end of the Hollow stays shut until the Ashen Verge is built.

title: A new Oakhaven Outpost
notes: Oakhaven Outpost is rebuilt and much less crowded: a cobbled square with the campfire and the waypoint, dirt roads and lamp posts to each part of the town, and room around everyone. The smith, the sage, the dyer and Corwin are in the west, the merchant, the gambler and Althea between the square and the river, and the Rift Gate and Captain Rourke are across the river by the bridge.
A river now runs through the town, and a raised terrace in the north holds the Battlemaster, the Stash Keeper and the Jeweler: climb the steps to reach them.
The Blackroot Wilds gets a river too, with two bridges, one of them on the way to the hunting lodge.
Maps can now have rivers with bridges, and raised terraces with stairs, so the next zones can have more depth.

title: Roads and lamp posts in the Wilds
notes: The Blackroot Wilds now has dirt roads leading from the gate to the waypoint, the glade, the hunting lodge and the ruined manor, cobblestone where they arrive, and lamp posts along them.
Maps can now carry paths on the ground, so the next zones will have them too.

title: Act I: The Bleeding Veil begins
notes: Act I is being rewritten as The Bleeding Veil. The outpost is now Oakhaven Outpost, and the first zone is the Blackroot Wilds: mist-choked woodland full of briarwolves, rotting villagers, ghouls, zombies and skeletons, with a hunting lodge and a ruined manor to find.

New main quest, The First Incursion: Battlemaster Brom sends you to cull the briarwolves at the gate and find Scout Captain Dennis, who is pinned in a hunting lodge by the Briarwolf Alpha. Take the Coagulated Rift Shard to High Priestess Althea.
New side quest, The Lost Heirloom: Merchant Corwin wants a lockbox from a ruined manor in the Wilds, and pays in an uncut gem. Read what is inside.
The Alpha is a boss fight of its own: it lunges and mauls, and its pack answers at half life. Like every quest boss it comes back for you to farm once the quest is handed in.
The old Ashwood quests, Into the Ashwood and The Lost Caravan, and Vesh are gone. Characters that finished them keep what they unlocked (the hirelings).

title: Tidier buttons
notes: The bag, options and passive tree buttons are now all icons of the same size.
The town portal scroll is an icon too, now just to the right of the mana globe at the bottom, with how many scrolls you have in its corner.

title: Vesh can be hurt
notes: Fixed: Vesh, and every boss with a fight of its own, stayed untouchable after his intro, so every attack said Immune. His protection now wears off by itself after the intro and each roar, as it was meant to.
His health bar no longer shows 101% at full life.

title: Hirelings and pets cross the boss ring
notes: The ring of fire round a boss fight no longer blocks your hireling, pet or allies: they walk through it, so one left outside can no longer get stuck there. It still seals you and the monsters in until the boss falls.

title: Bosses to farm
notes: Once you have handed in a quest, its boss is back for good: go back to the Ashwood and Vesh is at his camp again, with his rewards, every time you start the area afresh (leave, come back and choose Reset). The quest pays out once, as before.

title: Bigger party, tougher monsters, better rewards
notes: As in Diablo II, the more players there are in an area, the tougher its monsters: each extra player makes them take 60% more to kill. In return every kill gives each of you 35% more experience and drops come 25% more often and better, in zones and in rifts.
It counts the players in the area with you, so a party member in town changes nothing, and it follows people arriving and leaving. The party list shows what it comes to.

title: Gems and runes in their places
notes: The stash's Gems tab now has a fixed place for every gem: a row for each type (Ruby, Topaz, Emerald, Amethyst, Diamond) with its eight tiers along it, Chipped first. The ones you don't have are faint, and the count is at the top left of each.
Runes have a tab of their own, the whole ladder from El to Zod laid out in order, in the same way. The Jeweler shows both.

title: A currency tab like Path of Exile's
notes: The stash's Currency tab now gives every orb its own fixed place, in groups side by side (Basics, Rares and Special), with the count at the top left of each. An orb you have none of keeps its place as a faint slot, so you always know where to look.
The slots are bigger, so the whole grid shows at once, and hovering one names the orb.

title: No more weapon sets
notes: The weapon swap is gone: the button above the skills, the I / II switch on the character panel and the X key. If you had a second weapon set, its weapons are now in your bag.

title: Skill buttons in town
notes: The skill buttons now show in Ashfall Outpost too, greyed out, so the screen looks the same in town as out in the field. They do nothing there.

title: Loot on the ground
notes: Items on the ground are now just their picture, without the dark box and coloured border; the name above still shows the colour.
Magic and better items dropped by monsters, bosses and encounters now lie unidentified, as they do from a rift boss: their modifiers are hidden until you read a Scroll of Identify or visit the Sage.

title: A minimap
notes: A minimap in the top right corner shows where you've been, with you, the exits, the waypoint, people to talk to, things to use and the boss marked on it, and the monsters near you. Tap it (or press M) to see the whole map.
The bag and options are now icon buttons, to the left of the minimap, with the passives and town portal scroll beside them.
The party list is now on the left, under your hireling.

title: Areas stay as you left them
notes: When you leave an area by an exit, a waypoint or a town portal, it is still there when you come back: the monsters you killed stay dead and whatever lay on the ground is still lying there. An area only starts over when you leave the game.
If you go to an area you have already been in, a window asks whether to carry on where you left off or reset it, and tells you what is left. Reset brings back its monsters and boss.
A town portal always takes you back to the area it was opened in, as you left it, and back again.
If you die you wake at the waypoint in the same area. A boss fight you walked out of or died in starts over.
The Rift Gate asks the same if you left a rift unfinished through a town portal.

title: Boss fights
notes: Vesh, the Raider Captain, is now a proper boss fight. When he wakes he roars, a ring of fire seals round the camp, and his name and a health bar come up on screen.
His attacks are all shown on the ground first, so you can step out of the way: volleys of arrows, a long heavy shot, and rains of arrows landing around you. Stand in a warning and it hurts.
He fights in phases: at two-thirds and one-third of his life he roars (and can't be hurt for a moment), shouts, and calls his raiders. Take too long and he goes into a rage.
The ring opens when he falls, his raiders fall with him, and he drops better rewards. The camp has no ordinary monsters in it, so the fight is just him.
If you die, you wake at the waypoint and he's back at full life.

title: Pets
notes: Choose a pet in Options (the button under BAG): a hedgehog, snail, turtle, boar, monkey, mouse, crab, bee or bird. It trots along beside you and picks up the currency lying about, so you don't have to walk over and tap each pile.
It leaves your gear for you to pick, and it can't fight or be hurt, it's just company. Each character has their own.

title: More monsters, a wider view
notes: The camera is zoomed out a third, so you see more of the map around you. The new OPTIONS button under BAG opens a window where you can slide the view distance anywhere from far to close, and see it change as you move the slider.

Maps are much fuller: rifts and the Ashwood now have around three times the monsters, spread right across the map, so there's something to fight in every stretch. More packs also means more Elites and Legendaries to hunt.
A rift's packs sit in different places each run.

title: Password reset in Tainted's own words
notes: Forgot your password? on the sign-in screen opens a Tainted page, and the email it sends and the page it leads to speak of Tainted and send you back to the game.

title: Your own Tainted account
notes: Tainted is free and open to anyone: Create an account on the sign-in screen opens a Tainted sign-up page, and when it's done it sends you back to the game.
Delete account on the character screen removes your characters and your sign-in, after you confirm your password in the browser.
The sign-in screen's wording is about your Tainted account.

title: Random encounters, tidier loot
notes: Random encounters out in the campaign (about 1 visit in 2): a cottage in the woods whose zombies burst out when you come near, and a captive to free once they're dead; or cultists chanting round a summoning circle. Break the ritual before the 45 seconds are up (each cultist you kill buys time), or a Summoned Horror comes through.
What a fight drops of currency now lies in one pile you tap once, and a rift boss's orbs and shards are one pile, its gems and runes another.
Currency drops are less frequent and smaller.
Big trees and houses turn see-through when you stand behind them, so you never lose your character.
Currency, skill gem and shoulders slot changes from before are in this update too.

title: New skill icons
notes: New painted icons for the ranger, rogue and mage skills (Quick Shot, Power Shot, Multishot, Arrow Rain, Fan of Knives, Shadow Step, Death Blossom, Viper Strike, Firebolt, Meteor, Frost Nova, Arc, Arcane Ward, Thunderstorm, Holy Nova, Smite) and for the Scouts' skills.
Skill icons are a little smaller, so the slot borders and the round button rims show around them.

title: New gems and runes
notes: Socketed gems and runes now show on the item itself, down the middle of its icon in your bag and equipment, with dark rings for empty sockets. Select an item and its card shows each socket with its picture too, like Diablo 3.
Gems now come in 8 tiers like Diablo 3: Chipped, Flawed, Regular, Flawless, Star, Imperial, Royal and Flawless Royal. Three gems of a tier combine into the next at the Jeweler.
Five gem colours: Ruby, Topaz, Emerald, Amethyst and Diamond. Sapphires you had are now Rubies. Your old Perfect gems are now Star gems, just as strong.
New art for every gem and all 33 runes, El to Zod.

title: New currency icons
notes: New icons for Chaos, Exalted, Divine, Regal, Vaal, Alchemy, Jeweller's and Gemcutter's orbs, the Orb of Annulment, the Mirror of Kalandra, Armourer's Scrap, Blacksmith's Whetstone and the Town Portal scroll.

title: Bigger ring and amulet slots
notes: The ring and amulet slots on the character panel are now as big as the gloves and boots slots.

title: Wrists and legs
notes: Two new equipment slots, Wrists and Legs, with 16 new pieces: bracers, shorts, kilts and guards.
They drop like the rest of your gear and can be socketed, but they don't show on your character.

title: Shoulders slot
notes: The shoulders slot on the character panel is now as big as the gloves and boots slots.

title: Self-updating game
notes: The game now updates itself: new versions download when you connect, and the game restarts into them. No more installing the APK each time.
The phone version starts much faster.
Shoulders slot and 12 shoulder pieces, shown on your character.
One-handed crossbows with their own shooting animation.
Two-handed weapons, spears and daggers have their own animations.
Change how your armour and weapons look at the Dyer, using looks you have picked up. Unique items have their own looks.
The Gambler, Lucky Mott, sells unidentified items and restocks every so often.
Skill gems are chosen from dropdowns; drag gems onto items to socket them; drag an item to the empty screen to drop it.
